source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.habit: Usually a small tree; deciduous with thin foliage [Sophora identification key]
morphology_source_reported.inflorescence: Drooping racemes, conspicuous flowers partly obscured by new foliage
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Corollas 11–14 mm long; white standard changing pink, keel rose- to lavender-pink [key]
morphology_source_reported.fruits: Beadlike, irregularly constricted pods usually with 2–6 fertile segments, black when ripe and ca. 7–8 mm thick [key]

cautions: The source uses Sophora affinis, while inventory uses Styphnolobium affine; historical genus transfer requires independent confirmation
